topics.label: Introduction to the complement system lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic, contextualises its complexity, and outlines the scope of the session.

topics.label: Foundational principles, nomenclature, and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core concepts and molecular mechanics governing complement function, its naming rules, and the central role of C3 cleavage.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the upstream recognition pathways that drive the deposition and amplification of active C3b on target surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of activated complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream processes by which activated complement mediates pathogen clearance and inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation and self-protection against complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that prevent complement from activating on and damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct clinical presentations and pathologies resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion strategies and applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens evade complement-mediated destruction, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus and the practical applications of Protein A.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic marks the conclusion of the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
